newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - Key JGBs seen stabilising around 120.50.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Key JGBs seen stabilising around 120.50.

text.p: Key December 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are likely to stabilise around 120.50 on Wednesday after the topside was proven to be heavy at around 120.90 on Monday and Tuesday.
"People seem to be mostly satisfied with Tuesday's rise as high as 120.93 for now," said a dealer at a securities house. The contract's session high on Monday was 120.90.

The contract's downside room will also be limited as fears of a U.S. rate rise withered overnight, traders said. The rate fears were triggered by a rise in crude oil prices after news of a U.S. missile attack against Iraq on Tuesday.

"The contract could have risen to 121 without the U.S. attack yesterday," said a senior dealer at another securities house. Traders said if the December keeps above a five-day moving average of 120.58 on Wednesday, this may guarantee a short-term rising trend.

"Since the NAPM showed soft retail sales and oil prices did not rise too far yesterday, fears of an imminent U.S. rate rise have mostly faded," said a city bank analyst. "Such a change in sentiment may provide a place for investors to buy."
U.S. Treasuries ended higher on Tuesday on bargain-hunting and as soft retail sales spurred buying.
